requirement:
A file coverage map MUST identify each file by its workspace-relative path and
show its covered and instrumented line counts and percentage. These counts MUST
use the union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
restricted to the file and the records represented by that map, including
associated child processes. The map MUST visually distinguish coverage levels
while also displaying percentages as text. The percentage MUST describe the
map's recorded instrumented lines, rather than all physical source lines.

A listed file with instrumented lines but no positive execution counts MUST
show 0%. A listed file with no recorded instrumented lines in otherwise usable
coverage MUST show "not measured" without a percentage. Coverage whose
completeness cannot be established MUST be identified as unavailable rather
than as 0% or "not measured".
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map`. I did not read implementation source, because the supplied tests were enough to judge adequacy.

- **Path, counts and percentage.**
  - `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[file_maps_union_process_locations_and_filter_unexecuted_test_files]` asserts the per-file card for `code.rs` shows covered and instrumented counts plus a percentage. It checks the per-test detail map too.
  - `fn[file_map_escapes_paths_and_does_not_round_positive_coverage_to_zero]` checks a nested path is rendered escaped, and checks the count text.
- **Union rule with child processes.**
  - The first test gives a parent process and a child process with overlapping locations. Some counts are zero, one is positive in only one process, and one is `u64::MAX`.
  - The expected per-file result shows each location counted once in the denominator and counted as covered when any process has a positive count. It also shows child records are included, and that the map isn't averaged across processes.
  - The test also asserts the index total, so it checks the restriction to the file.
- **Percentage over instrumented lines, not physical lines.** `code.rs` has an uninstrumented comment line. The test expects the percentage over only the instrumented lines.
- **Visual distinction plus text.** The escape test checks the hsl background, `role="meter"`, `aria-valuenow` and the width style for zero, half and full coverage. It also checks the text percentage, including that a tiny positive value is shown as less than 0.1% and not as 0.
- **0% when instrumented but never executed.**
  - The first test checks `zero.rs` shows 0.0%.
  - `fn[maps_distinguish_no_runs_zero_hits_stale_and_incomplete_coverage]` checks a zero-hit record also shows 0.0%.
- **"not measured" without a percentage.** The first test checks `unmeasured.rs` shows "not measured" and contains no percent sign. The no-runs case in the second test also expects "not measured".
- **Unavailable rather than 0% or "not measured".**
  - The second test covers per-test maps with no processes, an attempt diagnostic, a process diagnostic, a missing captured source and an empty profile.
  - It also covers an incomplete child profile, stale source (changed and added files), unreadable source, and unreadable attempt metadata. The affected cards say unavailable with no percentage.
  - `fn[incomplete_attempts_do_not_label_their_files_as_unmeasured_in_a_partial_map]` checks a file touched only by an incomplete or stale attempt is "unavailable" and not "not measured", while a complete file still shows 100.0%.
- **Edge case.** An empty file list renders no file cards.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept. The color gradient is checked only for the presence of an hsl background, but the width and `aria-valuenow` assertions per level do distinguish levels. The text does not require a specific color mapping.

A file coverage map MUST identify each file by its workspace-relative path and
show its covered and instrumented line counts and percentage. These counts MUST
use the union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`,
restricted to the file and the records represented by that map, including
associated child processes. The map MUST visually distinguish coverage levels
while also displaying percentages as text. The percentage MUST describe the
map's recorded instrumented lines, rather than all physical source lines.
A listed file with instrumented lines but no positive execution counts MUST
show 0%. A listed file with no recorded instrumented lines in otherwise usable
coverage MUST show "not measured" without a percentage. Coverage whose
completeness cannot be established MUST be identified as unavailable rather
than as 0% or "not measured".
:::{req} index.summary
The coverage index MUST display the combined view selected under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`. It MUST identify the
contributing runs and show each selected test's binary, test name, attempt,
capture time, command, selection, and outcome, including missing or stale
coverage. It MUST show source revisions and uncommitted-source state when
available rather than present records from several runs as one run.
For first-party Rust files under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, the summary MUST compute
line coverage from the union of instrumented file-and-line locations in the
selected fresh records, including their associated child-process records.
Each location MUST count once in the denominator and count as covered when any
selected record has a positive execution count for it. Percentages MUST be
computed from those union counts rather than averaged across process reports.
A view with no instrumented lines MUST show coverage as unavailable. The index
MUST link to {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.details`, visibly identify
incomplete coverage, and MUST NOT imply that every current test has coverage
merely because all available records are valid.
